chunks: From him, from al-Hajjal, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Ghalib, from his father, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Ali ibn Abi Rafi', who said:
I was in charge of the treasury of Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام and was his scribe, and in his treasury there was a pearl necklace that had come into his possession on the day of al-Basrah.

He said: The daughter of Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام sent to me and said to me: I have been informed that in the treasury of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام there is a pearl necklace, and it is in your possession, and I would like you to lend it to me so that I may adorn myself with it during the days of Eid al-Adha. So I sent word to her that it would be a loan guaranteed and to be returned, O daughter of Amir al-Mu'minin. She said: Yes, a guaranteed loan to be returned after three days. So I handed it over to her. Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام saw it on her and recognized it, and he said to her: "From where did this necklace come to you?" She said: I borrowed it from Ali ibn Abi Rafi', the keeper of the treasury of Amir al-Mu'minin, so that I may adorn myself with it during the Eid, then return it. He said: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام then sent for me, and I came to him. He said to me: "Do you betray the Muslims, O son of Abi Rafi'?" I said to him: I seek refuge in Allah from betraying the Muslims. He said: "How did you lend the daughter of Amir al-Mu'minin the necklace that is in the treasury of the Muslims without my permission and their approval?" I said: O Amir al-Mu'minin, she is your daughter, and she asked me to lend it to her so she could adorn herself with it, so I lent it to her as a guaranteed loan to be returned. I guaranteed it from my own property, and it is upon me to return it sound to its place.

He said: "Then return it today, and beware of returning to the like of this, lest my punishment reach you." Then he said: "By Allah, if my daughter had taken the necklace other than as a guaranteed loan to be returned, then she would have been the first Hashimiyyah whose hand was cut for theft." He said: His statement reached his daughter, and she said to him: O Amir al-Mu'minin, I am your daughter and a part of you, so who has more right than I to wear it? Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said to her: "O daughter of Ali ibn Abi Talib, do not turn yourself away from the truth. Do all the women of the Muhajirin adorn themselves on this Eid with the like of this?" He said: So I took it back from her and returned it to its place.

key_terms.أَمِيرِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam Ali عليه السلام as leader of the faithful
key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ: the public treasury belonging to the Muslim community
key_terms.سَرِقَةٍ: theft, in the legal sense mentioned in the report
key_terms.عَارِيَّةً مَضْمُونَةً مَرْدُودَةً: a borrowed item whose return and compensation are guaranteed
key_terms.عُقُوبَتِي: my punishment; a warning of disciplinary consequence
key_terms.ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ: the Muslim community whose collective property rights are at issue

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali عليه السلام deal with his family regarding property from the public treasury?
ai.summary: This report narrates how Imam Ali عليه السلام objected when a necklace from the public treasury was lent to his daughter, even temporarily, without proper authorization. It highlights strict justice, protection of public wealth, and the Imam’s refusal to grant privilege to family members in matters involving the rights of the Muslims.
